learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: What political achievement does Plutarch attribute to Theseus?
Use the cited passage to explain: How should this claim be framed?

main.work: Plutarch: Lives of the Noble Grecians and Romans
main.author: Plutarch
main.translator: John Dryden and others; revised by Arthur Hugh Clough
main.locator: Life of Theseus, unification of Attica; local text, normalized characters 40458-40761
main.excerpt: together all the inhabitants of Attica into one town, and made them one people of one city, whereas before they lived dispersed, and were not easy to assemble upon any affair for the common interest. Nay, differences and even wars often occurred between them, which he by his persuasions appeased, going
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Plutarch credits Theseus with bringing the inhabitants of Attica into one political community. The story presents a founder of civic order, not merely a monster-killer; it is a later biography’s account of a legendary past.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “together all the inhabitants of Attica into one town, and made them one people of one city, whereas before they lived dispersed, and were not easy to assemble upon any affair for the common interest. Nay, differences and even wars often occurred between them, which he by his persuasions appeased, going”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: The hero becomes a civic argument. Athens can explain its unity by placing that unity inside a legendary founder’s actions.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Say that Plutarch credits Theseus with civic unification. That wording preserves the distinction between a later foundation narrative and contemporary documentation of how Athens developed.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: A founder is useful because the city can borrow his authority for its own origins.

quiz.prompt: How should this claim be framed?

choices.text: As a surviving law written by Theseus himself
As an episode narrated by Achilles in the Iliad
As Plutarch’s legendary foundation narrative, not contemporary documentation
